messages:
kevin: heads-up — canary for mixtral-8b kernel-picker rolled yesterday and we're seeing 20-30% p95 latency regression on chat workloads that use system prompts with special tokens :eyes:

maria: saw that in the dashboard, looks correlated with sequences that hit byte-fallback tokenization (lots of emojis/symbols)

kevin: my hypothesis: tokenizer produces slightly different token boundaries which shifts KV alignment and causes kernel-picker to choose a heavy dense kernel instead of the smaller heads-optimized path when seq_len > ~512

alex: do we have profiler traces? nvprof / nsight or perf events that show extra matmul or memcpy during kv concat?

maria: attaching quick snippet from the canary run (nvprof summary):

maria: ```
== Profiling result: mixtral-8b-canary
Time(%)  Calls  Avg ms  Name
 40.2%     12   3.8ms   cudaMatMul_v2
 22.7%     48   1.2ms   kv_cache_write
 15.9%     96   0.6ms   tokenize_byte_fallback
 12.1%     24   0.9ms   kernel_switch_dispatch
  9.1%     30   0.4ms   memcpy_async
```

maria: shows extra overhead in tokenize + kv write for affected traces

toni: could this be RoPE scaling related? if tokenizer boundaries change, the token index offsets used for RoPE math can cause different attention mask and head codepath choices if we base heuristics on effective pos enc distribution

kevin: exactly — we saw subtle shifts in ``pos_idx`` histogram. small change in avg pos bumped a few requests over the kernel_picker threshold that prefers the large-kv kernel (which has worse single-stream latency)

alex: timeline: kernel-picker change 2026-03-10 switched to heuristics: prefer dense kernel when avg_heads*avg_seq_len > 2048. That threshold interacts poorly with variable token counts introduced by byte fallback

yu: quick mitigation: canonicalize system prompts to avoid byte-fallback chars (pre-normalize emojis -> token equivalents) or run a fast tokenizer-normalize pass that forces consistent token boundaries before kernel selection

kevin: we tried a hotfix last night: pre-tokenize step added to picker; reduced p95 by ~12% on canary but added 0.8ms to median due to extra tokenize call

maria: perf diffs from canary after hotfix: p50 -0.2ms, p95 -12%, cpu cost +3% (extra tokenization CPU), gpu time down by ~8%

toni: longer-term we should decouple kernel choice from raw token count -> use sampled kv-density estimate from first N tokens in request (cheap sketch) rather than full seq_len which can be noisy because of tokenizer variance

alex: agree. also consider making kernel-picker robust to RoPE shift: compute effective_rope_span = max(windowed_pos_idx) and use that instead of avg_pos*heads heuristic

deploy-bot: canary metrics: mixtral-8b-picker-v2 -> rollout at 10% started 2026-03-11T02:12Z, p95 latency spike detected at 2026-03-11T06:04Z, auto-pause triggered

infra-bot: logs /correlate: requests with emoji-heavy system prompts had 3.4x higher probability of selecting large-kv kernel than ascii-only prompts

yu: proposed quick PR: "tokenizer: normalize_specials_for_picker" — do pre-tokenize & fingerprint tokens used only by picker; no change to downstream cache keys so KV remains stable

kevin: can we ensure pre-tokenize doesn't affect cache key? we already observed cache fragmentation when we touched upstream tokenizer mapping last year

maria: note: for canary we intentionally DID NOT change cache keys. the pre-tokenize output used only for a side-channel heuristic. cache keys unchanged. confirmed in logs

toni: next steps I suggest:
- short: roll forward hotfix to 30% canary, monitor p95 + cpu cost
- medium: implement sampled kv-density estimator + update kernel-picker heuristic to use effective_rope_span
- long: add tokenizer instrumentation to surface byte-fallback ratio per request in trace logs

alex: ack. I'll draft the kv-density sketch proposal and a fallback threshold sweep test matrix (include mixtral/llama/qwen configs)

kevin: thanks team. @maria can you post the canary diff and the minimal reproducer (system prompt + user message) in the thread so SRE can run local perf checks? :thumbsup:

maria: on it. minimal repro in case someone wants to run locally:

maria: ```
# repro: long chat with emoji system prompt
system = "You are an assistant. \uD83D\uDE0A\nUse short replies."
user = "Explain amortized complexity of batching in simple terms."
# run: python perf_local.py --model mixtral-8b --prompt-file repro.json --profile nvprof
```

yu: tagging follow-ups: I'll open the "picker-normalize-for-tokenizer" PR and include unit tests that confirm no cache-key changes

kevin: perfect. if we can get 30% canary stable then we can run threshold grid overnight and ship a permanent solver next week

maria: uploading nvprof traces + flamegraphs to the ticket now: https://redwood-internal/issue/INF-4827 :link:

kevin: great. closing the loop here — thanks everyone.
